papers.title: Framing Anomaly in Lattice Chern-Simons-Maxwell Theory
papers.abstract: Framing anomaly is a key property of ( 2 + 1 ) d chiral topological orders, for it reveals that the chirality is an intrinsic bulk property of the system, rather than a property that requires a boundary between two systems. Understanding framing anomaly in lattice models is particularly interesting, as concrete, solvable lattice models of chiral topological orders are rare. In a previous work [Z.-A. Xu and J.-Y. Chen, .], we defined and solved the U(1) Chern-Simons-Maxwell theory on spacetime lattice, showing its chiral edge mode and the associated gravitational anomaly on boundary. In this Letter, we show its framing anomaly in the absence of boundary by computing the expectation of a lattice version of the modular T operator in the ground subspace on a spatial torus, from which we extract that ⟨ T ⟩ has a universal phase of − 2 π / 12 as expected: − 2 π / 8 from the Gauss-Milgram sum of the topological spins of the ground states, and 2 π / 24 from the framing anomaly. We can also extract the 2 π / 24 framing anomaly phase alone from the full spectrum of T in the ground subspace by computing ⟨ T m ⟩ . This pins down the last and most crucial property required for a valid lattice definition of U(1) Chern-Simons theory.

papers.title: Three-Dimensional Topological Ferroelectrics
papers.authors: Haohao Sheng, Sheng Zhang, Zhong Fang, Hongming Weng, Zhijun Wang
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) topological ferroelectric (FE) insulators, in which topological and FE orders naturally coexist, enable field-controlled spintronic devices. In this work, we predict a new structure of bismuth monohalides Bi4Br4 and Bi4I4, denoted $γ$ phase, and demonstrate that it is an ideal 3D topological FE insulator. Systematic first-principles calculations confirm the stability and synthesizability of $γ$-Bi4X4 (X=Br, I). Although the noncentrosymmetric $γ$ phase crystallizes in the space group $Cmc2_1$ with no symmetry-based classifications/indicators, the nontrivial topology can be characterized by the spin Chern number (SCN). Spin-resolved Wilson loops show the $s_z$ SCN $C_{s_z}=2$, indicating the spin-resolved topology of a 3D quantum spin Hall insulator state. The $z$-direction polarization can be switched by interlayer sliding, requiring only crossing a small energy barrier. Finally, we design an electrically controlled spin-filter device on bilayer films that can generate a switchable spin-polarized current. Combining a single-phase crystal, a sizable band gap, and robust band topology against FE switching, these bismuth monohalides serve as a prototype of intrinsic 3D topological FE insulators, providing an ideal platform for realizing new nonvolatile functionalities in spintronic devices.

papers.title: Quantized even number of vortices in a confined PTO/STO ferroelectric heterostructure with edge pinning effect
papers.authors: Guanshihan Du, Peiran Tong, Yuhui Huang, Yongjun Wu, Juan Li, He Tian, Zijian Hong
papers.abstract: Polar vortices in ferroelectric heterostructures exhibit rich physical phenomena, but controlling their number and stability remains challenging. We investigate polar vortices in laterally confined lead titanate slabs embedded in a strontium titanate matrix on a dysprosium scandate substrate. Phase-field simulations and transmission electron microscopy show that lateral confinement favors discrete, even numbers of vortices. Energy analysis attributes this preference to competition among Landau, elastic, electrostatic and gradient contributions. Simulations and in situ electrical biasing observations further reveal that polar vortices near slab edges remain stable while interior regions switch under applied field, and vortex configurations recover after the applied voltage is removed. Here, we show that lateral confinement and edge pinning provide a route to controlling the number and switching behavior of polar vortices in ferroelectric heterostructures. The authors show that lateral confinement favors even numbers of polar vortices in ferroelectric heterostructures and that edge pinning stabilizes vortices during electrical switching.

papers.title: Twist-angle-dependent quantum phase diagrams in moiré bilayer MoTe2
papers.authors: Zheng Sun, Fan Xu, Jiayi Li, Yifan Jiang, Jingjing Gao, Cheng Xu, Tongtong Jia, Kehao Cheng, Shaozheng Wang, Wanghao Tian, Jinyang Zhang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Jinfeng Jia, Shengwei Jiang, Yang Zhang, Yuanbo Zhang, Shiming Lei, Xiaoxue Liu, Tingxin Li
papers.abstract: Two-dimensional semiconducting moiré superlattices provide a highly tunable platform for investigating strongly correlated and topological quantum phases1–5. As a prototypical example, twisted bilayer MoTe2 (tMoTe2) has been shown to host fractional topological phases at zero magnetic field6–20. However, their evolution with twist angle and competition with other correlated quantum states remain largely unexplored. Here we report a systematic transport study of twist-angle-dependent phase diagrams in tMoTe2 across a range of 3.79°–5.76°, revealing an evolution from valley-polarized, fractional topological states to valley-degenerate correlated states and superconductivity. At relatively small twist angles, partially filled Chern bands of tMoTe2 host fractional quantum anomalous Hall states following the Jain sequence, together with signatures of an anomalous composite Fermi liquid at moiré hole filling factor νh = 1/2. Increasing twist angle progressively suppresses fractional topological phases and reconstructs the half-filled Chern band into symmetry-breaking integer Chern insulating states. At νh = 1, we observe a transition from robust integer quantum anomalous Hall insulators at small angles to displacement-field-tuned, topologically trivial correlated insulators at larger angles. At twist angles above approximately 5.6°, superconductivity emerges adjacent to the νh = 1 correlated insulator, with a phase diagram closely resembling that recently reported in twisted bilayer WSe2 (refs. 21–24). Our results indicate a unified twist-angle-driven phase evolution linking fractional topology, symmetry breaking, magnetic order and superconductivity, providing new insight into the emergent quantum phenomena in moiré systems. Twist-angle-dependent studies of moiré bilayer MoTe2 reveal a transition from fractional topological states to correlated insulators and superconductivity, linking topology, symmetry breaking and magnetism in moiré quantum materials.

papers.abstract: We address a central open question in driven topological matter by investigating the nonequilibrium response of a two-dimensional magnet with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions subjected to a periodically oscillating magnetic field. Using extensive Monte Carlo simulations, we uncover a dynamically reentrant skyrmion phase that emerges within a finite window of field amplitudes and bias fields, sandwiched between the conventional skyrmion and polarized ferromagnetic phases. This phase has no equilibrium counterpart and originates from an imbalance between skyrmion creation and annihilation over a single field cycle, leading to a reversal of the period-averaged topological charge. We show that the re-entrant phase exists only in the dynamic response regime where the system can follow the drive, and is suppressed at higher driving frequencies. Our results establish periodic driving as a nonequilibrium control parameter for stabilizing and reversing skyrmion topology.

papers.relevance_reason: This is original theory of a driven magnetic texture in a two-dimensional magnet, with a substantive prediction about nonequilibrium skyrmion phases.

papers.abstract: We investigate the magnetic states of the Shastry-Sutherland-lattice magnet NdB$_4$ using single-crystal neutron diffraction. We focus on magnetic fields applied along the tetragonal $c$ axis, which stabilise the fractional 1/5~magnetisation plateau. In the low-temperature phase below 4.9 K, the transition into the plateau state at approximately 12 kOe is marked by a change in the propagation vectors from $(1/5,0,-2/5)$ and its double $(2/5,0,1/5)$ to $(0,0,1/5)$ and $(0,0,2/5)$. At the transition from the plateau to a nominally `field-polarised' state near 33 kOe, all magnetic reflections associated with non-integer propagation vectors disappear, whereas reflections corresponding to the $\mathbf{k}=0$ component persist throughout the entire field range. We conclude that that the in-plane components survive even in the high-field phase and that the polarisation is, in fact, incomplete. The observed field dependence provides direct support for a description of NdB$_4$ in terms of two coupled magnetic instabilities: all-in-all-out order of the in-plane moments and a spin-density wave of the out-of-plane components.

papers.relevance_reason: Neutron diffraction directly resolves field-dependent magnetic order in a frustrated quantum magnet and establishes a substantive result about its high-field state.

Near 33 kOe, at the transition to the nominally field-polarised state, reflections associated with non-integer propagation vectors disappear, but the k = 0 component persists throughout the measured field range. The authors infer that in-plane moment components survive in the high-field phase, so the polarisation is incomplete. papers.abstract: Periodic driving enables ultrafast control of electronic structures in solids through the formation of photon-dressed Floquet-Bloch states. However, the measured photoemission spectra are influenced not only by these states but also by their interference with Volkov-dressed outgoing photoelectrons. Here, we demonstrate that Floquet-Volkov interference can generate spin-polarized photoemission in a collinear antiferromagnetic Dirac model without spin-orbit coupling (SOC). An in-plane linearly polarized pump preserves $\mathcal{PT}$ symmetry, leaving the Floquet quasienergies spin degenerate. Under near-resonant driving, photon-dressed conduction and valence bands hybridize, producing spin-dependent relative phases that are converted into unequal spin-resolved photoemission intensities through interference between pathways reaching the same Volkov-dressed final state. We analytically identify this interference mechanism and verify it using nonequilibrium Green-function calculations under periodic driving and finite pump-probe pulses. We further demonstrate that rotating the probe polarization can suppress or reverse the spin polarization without modifying the Floquet bands. Our findings establish Floquet-Volkov interference as a route to spin-selective photoemission in driven antiferromagnets without Floquet spin splitting or SOC.

papers.abstract: Classical spin liquids are characterized by an extensive number of ground-state configurations. Coulomb spin liquids have, in this ground-state manifold, a divergence-free local constraint, which gives dipolar correlations and pinch points in the structure factor. Recently, models with a complementary ground-state constraint, defined by a zero-circulation constraint (Ampère's law), have been proposed. While classical Coulomb spin liquids forbid emergent charges, their Ampère counterparts leave the charges unconstrained. Here we study an Ising Ampère model on the octochlore lattice. The ground states obey a Gauss law for an antisymmetric rank-two field, i.e., three coupled two-dimensional Gauss laws, which are expected to produce pinch points in the structure factor. Nevertheless, maximal charges, vertices with all six arrows in or out, spontaneously accumulate on one of the two sublattices of the cubic lattice, with disordered signs. This order has a purely entropic origin; it washes out the pinch-point singularities at large scales, produces no magnetic Bragg peaks, and coexists with an extensive entropy. The system enters into this sublattice long-range ordered state through a continuous transition in what seems to be the three-dimensional Ising universality class. Moreover, the state has no magnetic order; it is even under time reversal: it is a hidden, entropic order within the Ampère manifold. Thus, a system whose Gauss law would predict an algebraic spin liquid becomes, through a non-magnetic ordering transition, a partially ordered short-range spin liquid. Our study is based on a combination of the constraint-vector theory, exact bounds and enumeration, and Monte Carlo, Wang-Landau, and parallel-tempering simulations.
papers.physics_advance: In the classical Ampère spin liquid, an entropic transition produces sublattice order of maximal emergent charges with disordered signs; this hidden order suppresses large-scale pinch points while preserving extensive entropy and the absence of magnetic order.
papers.relevance_reason: This is original condensed-matter theory of spin-liquid states, establishing a nonmagnetic ordering phenomenon and its effects on correlations and pinch points.

papers.abstract: Spin swapping converts a primary spin current into a secondary one by interchanging its flow and spin-polarization directions, attributed to spin-orbit scattering or spin-band splitting. Here we uncover a fundamentally distinct route to spin swapping arising from the orbital degree of freedom in the spin pumping to centrosymmetric multiorbital materials \textit{without spin-band splitting}. When the dynamical proximity ferromagnet injects a longitudinal spin current flowing normal to the interface, spin-orbit-entangled orbital textures redirect the injected spins into longitudinal and transverse orbital currents. Their subsequent conversion back to the spin sector generates transverse spin currents with propagation and polarization directions swapped relative to the primary spin current. The swapping efficiency achieves $50\%$ for Ge and Si. Governed by a fourth-rank tensor constrained by crystalline symmetry and without requiring spin-orbit scattering or inversion symmetry breaking, our finding reveals spin-orbital textures as hidden intermediate channels of spin swapping with unexplored material choices and functionalities.

papers.abstract: The quantized Hall effect is the textbook emblem of universality: a resistance fixed by $h/e^2$, apparently indifferent to the shape of the sample, to its edges and to the direction of the current. That indifference is only half true. The plateau value is universal; the plateau is not. In a gate-defined Hall bar with one hard and one soft edge, reversing the current moves the plateau edge, and exchanging the edges reverses the move. We identify the symmetry that forces this. Because a perpendicular field breaks time reversal, the relevant operation is the in-plane $C_2$ rotation; within the self-consistent screening model it gives the covariance relation $R_α[B,V_{\mathrm{conf}}(x),I]=R_α[B,V_{\mathrm{conf}}(-x),-I]$, exact deep in the nonlinear regime and independent of linear response or microscopic reversibility. It predicts a rectification that is odd under exchange of the gate voltages and reverses with the magnetic field. The field-reversal test leaves the frozen lateral disorder untouched, so it holds for a single sample; it has not yet been performed. A further measurement, collapsing one incompressible strip, discriminates between co-directed and chiral pictures of the current. Self-consistent calculations show the soft-edge strip widening from 69 to 106\,nm on current reversal, moving the Hall resistance from 0.940 to $0.999994\,h/2e^2$ within a bounded window in magnetic field. The effect is a gate-tunable vector-product nonreciprocity, not magnetochiral anisotropy.
papers.physics_advance: A symmetry relation links current reversal to exchanging the hard and soft edges, predicting gate-tunable Hall-resistance rectification and a reversal of the effect with magnetic field.
papers.relevance_reason: This is original theory of nonlinear transport in a quantum Hall material, with testable predictions for how edge asymmetry controls current-dependent plateaus.

papers.abstract: Fractional quantum Hall (FQH) edges with proximity-induced superconductivity can host parafermionic zero modes (PZMs), making them a promising platform for topological quantum computing. Recent experiments [Gül et al., Phys. Rev. X 12, 021057 (2022)] measured the edge conductance from crossed Andreev reflection (CAR) between counter-propagating FQH edges separated by a narrow superconductor. The observed conductance was small and non-quantized, with two distinct behaviors: some states show temperature-independent conductance, while others show conductance that grows as temperature decreases. We explain these results by dissipation to sub-gap modes in the superconductor and present a phase diagram for the FQH-superconductor junction. We show that for Jain states, temperature-independent non-quantized conductance occurs only in the presence of an integer mode (such as at filling $ν=1\pm\frac{1}{m}$, with odd $m\geq3$) strongly coupled to the dissipative channel. The predicted temperature trends qualitatively agree with the experiment, which shows temperature-independent conductance for $ν=2/3$ and integer states, but not for $ν=1/3$ and $ν=2/5$. We propose comparing $ν=4/3$ and $2/3$ to test the predicted influence of the relative chirality of integer and fractional modes.

papers.abstract: Lanthanum polyhydrides, synthesized under extreme pressure, exhibit near-room-temperature superconductivity. Finding a precise arrangement of the hydrogen sublattice that is critical for understanding the strong electron-phonon coupling remains experimentally unresolved due to the small X-ray scattering form factor of hydrogen atoms. In this work, we attempt to computationally reconstruct hydrogen sublattices of the LaH$_{12}$ at 100-200 GPa combining unconstrained evolutionary searches and structure generation with fixed lanthanum sublattice. By implementing a similarity metric, we screen the computationally generated configurations against experimental powder X-ray diffraction data. We specifically identify the trigonal $R\bar{3}$-LaH$_{12}$ and pseudo-hexagonal $C222_1$-La$_2$H$_{24}$ phases, which demonstrate close agreement with the experimental X-ray diffraction data. First-principles calculations confirm the metallic and superconducting nature of these hydrides. Crucially, our lattice dynamics analysis using the stochastic self-consistent harmonic approximation (SSCHA) indicates that these structures are dynamically stable. We reveal the presence of molecular H$_2$ units and soft phonon modes in the trigonal LaH$_{12}$ that suppresses superconductivity ($T_c \ge 30$ K), while the hydrogen clathrate network in the $C222_1$ phase drives strong electron-phonon interactions, yielding the coupling parameters of $λ\approx 1.83$, $ω_{\log} \approx 87.5$ meV and transition temperature of $T_c\approx 150$ K at 150 GPa.

papers.abstract: Whether $d$-wave or $s_\pm$-wave pairing prevails in the bilayer nickelate \ce{La3Ni2O7} remains unresolved, and how its observed spin order and magnetic excitations relate to the pairing mechanism is unclear. Here, we use finite-temperature determinant quantum Monte Carlo simulations of a minimal bilayer Hubbard model to investigate pairing competition at strong interlayer coupling, where intralayer and interlayer antiferromagnetic correlations have comparable strengths. We find that spin stripes develop spontaneously with increasing hole doping, accompanied by a crossover of the dominant pairing symmetry from $d$-wave to $s_\pm$-wave. The crossover tracks the changing relative strengths of the spin correlations, with the interlayer correlations overtaking their intralayer counterparts in magnitude. Concomitantly, the dynamical spin structure factor exhibits a momentum-dependent reorganization of the magnetic excitations, consistent with fluctuating spin stripes. Our results identify the structure of spin fluctuations as a key link between spin stripes and pairing competition, offering a minimal-model perspective for understanding \ce{La3Ni2O7}.
papers.physics_advance: The calculations find doping-induced spin stripes alongside a crossover from d-wave to s±-wave pairing, associated with a shift from dominant intralayer to interlayer spin correlations and a reorganization of magnetic excitations.
papers.relevance_reason: Determinant quantum Monte Carlo on a bilayer Hubbard model yields predictions about spin order, pairing competition, and magnetic excitations relevant to a correlated nickelate.

papers.abstract: We develop a microscopic theory of anyon superconductivity that connects electronic interactions in a lightly doped Laughlin state to the universal physics of a resonantly interacting anyon gas. Using geometric quantization of Laughlin quasiholes, we derive the effective many-body Hamiltonian of dilute charge-$2e/3$ anyons, including their valley structure, dispersion, and statistical and short-range interactions, together with an explicit map between anyon and electron observables. This reduces the dilute many-body problem to a few parameters fixed by data computable from few anyon numerics. In analogy with resonant Fermi and Bose gases, we organize the dilute anyon problem around a two-body binding resonance and its relevant and marginal perturbations. For a three-valley gas of charge-$2e/3$ anyons, we identify a resonance whose long-distance theory is governed by an Aharonov-Casher anyon Hamiltonian whose magnetic field is the statistical Chern-Simons field and whose ground state is exactly solvable. Using the ground state wavefunction, we demonstrate Cooper-pair off-diagonal long-range order directly in electron coordinates and determine the pairing symmetry and vortex-lattice structure. The leading perturbations at the fixed point are a relevant pair detuning and a marginal three-body contact in the valley-singlet channel, which determine the compressibility and sound velocity. A repulsive three-body coupling is marginally irrelevant, allowing the fixed point to control a parametrically broad dilute regime near pair resonance, while attractive three-body interactions instead generate charge-$2e$ trimers. More broadly, our results show that binding thresholds between competing anyon composites host universal resonant regimes that are not captured by the lowest-energy anyon species alone, providing a new setting for controlled theories of anyon matter.
papers.physics_advance: Identifies a resonant dilute anyon regime with an exactly solvable ground state exhibiting electron-pair off-diagonal long-range order, and determines its pairing symmetry, vortex lattice, and leading perturbations.
papers.relevance_reason: This is an original theory of correlated anyons and superconductivity in a doped Laughlin state, with a controlled resonant regime and concrete pairing predictions.
papers.summary_zh: 作者建立微观理论，将稀释的电荷 2e/3 Laughlin 准空穴与共振相互作用任意子气体联系起来，并给出任意子与电子观测量之间的明确映射。对于三谷气体，作者识别出一个具有精确可解长距离基态的共振，并展示了电子坐标下的 Cooper 对非对角长程序。
papers.method_en: Using geometric quantization of Laughlin quasiholes, the authors derive an effective many-body Hamiltonian that includes valley structure, dispersion, statistics, and short-range interactions, along with a map to electron observables. They organize the dilute-gas theory around a two-body binding resonance and analyze its long-distance Aharonov–Casher anyon Hamiltonian, ground-state wavefunction, and leading perturbations.
papers.method_zh: 作者利用 Laughlin 准空穴的几何量子化推导有效多体哈密顿量，其中包含谷自由度、色散、统计性质和短程相互作用，并建立与电子观测量的映射。研究围绕二体束缚共振组织稀薄气体理论，并分析其长距离 Aharonov–Casher 任意子哈密顿量、基态波函数和主要微扰。
papers.result_en: For a three-valley gas of charge-2e/3 anyons, the identified resonance has a long-distance theory governed by an Aharonov–Casher anyon Hamiltonian whose magnetic field is the statistical Chern–Simons field; its ground state is exactly solvable. From this wavefunction, the authors demonstrate Cooper-pair off-diagonal long-range order directly in electron coordinates and determine the pairing symmetry and vortex-lattice structure. They find that the leading perturbations are a relevant pair detuning and a marginal valley-singlet three-body contact, which determine compressibility and sound velocity. A repulsive three-body coupling is marginally irrelevant and permits a parametrically broad dilute regime near resonance, whereas attractive three-body interactions generate charge-2e trimers. More generally, the work argues that binding thresholds between competing anyon composites can host universal resonant regimes not captured by considering only the lowest-energy anyon species.
papers.result_zh: 对于电荷 2e/3 的三谷任意子气体，所识别的共振具有由 Aharonov–Casher 任意子哈密顿量支配的长距离理论，其中磁场为统计性的 Chern–Simons 场，且其基态可精确求解。作者利用该波函数直接在电子坐标中证明 Cooper 对非对角长程序，并确定配对对称性和涡旋晶格结构。研究发现，主要微扰是相关的成对失谐和边缘的谷单态三体接触相互作用，它们决定压缩率和声速。排斥性三体耦合在重整化群意义下边缘无关，使共振附近存在参数上宽广的稀薄区域；吸引性三体相互作用则会生成电荷 2e 三聚体。更一般地，作者指出，不同任意子复合体之间的束缚阈值可能产生普适共振区，而仅考虑最低能任意子种类无法描述这些区域。
papers.future_en: A natural follow-up is to compute the few-anyon parameters that fix the effective theory and test whether the predicted broad resonant regime is accessible in a specific Laughlin-state platform. Measurements of pairing and vortex-lattice properties could further examine the predicted electron-coordinate order; the abstract does not report such experiments.
papers.future_zh: 自然的后续工作是计算用于确定有效理论参数的少任意子性质，并检验特定 Laughlin 态平台是否能够实现理论预测的宽广共振区。对配对和涡旋晶格性质的测量可进一步检验所预测的电子坐标序；摘要未报告此类实验。
papers.tier_reason_en: The abstract presents a controlled microscopic route from Laughlin quasiholes to resonant anyon matter, an exactly solvable three-valley resonance, and explicit electron-coordinate superconducting order, together with a broader universality claim. This combination of conceptual scope and concrete theoretical results supports a PRL-level assessment.
papers.tier_reason_zh: 摘要提出了从 Laughlin 准空穴到共振任意子物质的受控微观理论，给出可精确求解的三谷共振和明确的电子坐标超导序，并提出更广泛的普适性结论。其概念范围与具体理论结果的结合支持评为 PRL 档次。
